AlertFeedback.description: What the care team said about an alert. Logged, and it moves the threshold.

cause.description: The optional answer to "what was it?" (SPEC section 5, MVP 8): a pattern_id from the pattern library, 'other' for a cause the library has no pattern for, or null when nobody said.
cause.title: Cause

AlertFeedback.title: AlertFeedback

AlertKind.description: How urgent the flag is: two bad sessions in 24-48 h, or a slow upward drift.
AlertKind.title: AlertKind

BaselineComparison.description: This resident's own history against what just happened (SPEC section 7).

baseline_days.description: Days of history the baseline is built from.
baseline_days.title: Baseline Days

threshold.description: This resident's current threshold, tuned by feedback.
threshold.title: Threshold

BaselineComparison.title: BaselineComparison

ErrorType.description: The everyday-action error types in SPEC section 7.
ErrorType.title: ErrorType

EvidenceKind.description: What a piece of evidence points at. Never a video clip (SPEC section 8).
EvidenceKind.title: EvidenceKind

EvidenceRef.description:
A pointer to evidence already stored: a step event, or a span of the skeleton
replay. Never a video clip (SPEC section 8).

event_id.description: Set when kind is step_event: the StepEvent it refers to.
event_id.title: Event Id

EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef

FeedbackVerdict.description: The nurse's answer to an alert, which tunes this resident's threshold.
FeedbackVerdict.title: FeedbackVerdict

PatternMatch.description:
One pattern a flagged change is consistent with (SPEC section 7.5).

A flag says *something* changed; these say what kind of change it looks like, so
the care team knows what to rule out first. Scored by deterministic rules over
features the pipeline already has (`routine_watch.patterns`) against a library of
patterns held as data (`routine_watch.patterns_library`), so the wording is always
"consistent with ... - consider ruling out ...", and an empty list is a real
answer: a change was detected with no clear pattern.

pattern_id.description: The pattern in the library, e.g. 'sudden_change'.
pattern_id.title: Pattern Id

name.description: How the pattern is shown to a nurse.
name.title: Name

evidence.description: Plain-language lines read off the features, e.g. 'omissions up to 1.0 a session from 0.0'.
evidence.title: Evidence

checks.description: What to rule out, from the library: a shared SuggestedCheck where one fits, otherwise the pattern's own wording.
checks.title: Checks

PatternMatch.title: PatternMatch

PatternUrgency.description: How soon a pattern wants a human to look (SPEC section 7.5).
PatternUrgency.title: PatternUrgency

SuggestedCheck.description: Checks an alert may suggest to the care team (SPEC section 6.4).
SuggestedCheck.title: SuggestedCheck

TaskError.description: One everyday-action error found in a session (SPEC section 7).

step_id.description: The step the error is about. Null only when no single step applies.
step_id.title: Step Id

self_corrected.description: The resident fixed it straight away: a weaker signal, not a full error.
self_corrected.title: Self Corrected

TaskError.title: TaskError

TimeOfDay.description:
Which part of a day a session started in (SPEC section 7.5).

The three parts a nurse reads off a shift rather than clock hours, so "errors
only late in the day" is something an alert can show rather than only say:
morning before noon, afternoon until 17:00, evening from 17:00 on.
TimeOfDay.title: TimeOfDay

TimeOfDayErrors.description:
One part of the day, counted over the two weeks behind an alert (SPEC section
7.5).

`sessions` is how many sessions this resident started in that part of the day and
`errors` how many errors those sessions had between them, so a reader can tell
"three bad evenings" from "one evening, three errors". Both are counts over this
resident's own history, not rates: the strip is evidence a nurse reads, and the
rate is already in the pattern's own evidence lines.

sessions.description: Sessions started in this part of the day, assisted ones left out.
sessions.title: Sessions

errors.description: Errors in those sessions, self-corrected slips left out - the same count the session score and this resident's normal are built from (SPEC section 7).
errors.title: Errors

TimeOfDayErrors.title: TimeOfDayErrors

description:
A change flagged for a human to review (SPEC section 7).

Routine Watch flags a change and shows the evidence behind it. It never diagnoses.

session_ids.description: The sessions behind the flag. A single bad session never alerts.
session_ids.title: Session Ids

summary.description: Plain language, written from the detected evidence only.
summary.title: Summary

patterns.description: The patterns this change is consistent with, best first (at most 3). Empty means a change was detected with no clear pattern.
patterns.title: Patterns

feedback.description: Null until a nurse confirms it or calls it a false alarm.

errors_by_time_of_day.description: Errors and sessions per part of the day over the two weeks before the alert, one entry per bucket: the visible evidence behind an evening-only pattern (SPEC section 7.5). Read off the resident's own session history by the route that serves the alert (`routine_watch.api_alerts`), so it is null on a stored record and on a resident with no sessions in that window.
errors_by_time_of_day.title: Errors By Time Of Day
